title: AgenTest: Mining Business Rules to Test LLM Agents for Business Logic Bugs
abstract: arXiv:2610.28116v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly execute business operations through tools and interact directly with application data and services. Beyond completing user requests, these agents must obey domain-specific business rules that constrain when actions are permitted and what data or resources may be affected. Violating such rules can lead to business logic bugs, even when a task appears successful. Detecting these bugs is difficult because the rules are rarely available as explicit, testable specifications. They are distributed across system prompts and tool definitions, while others remain implicit in domain knowledge. Existing agent testing approaches typically evaluate task success, predefined policies, or known attack scenarios. This limits their ability to systematically uncover previously unspecified business-rule violations.   We present AgenTest, which mines business rules from system prompts, tool definitions, and domai

translated_title: AgenTest：挖掘业务规则以测试LLM智能体的业务逻辑缺陷
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLM）智能体越来越多地通过工具执行业务操作，并直接与应用数据和服务进行交互。除了完成用户请求之外，这些智能体还必须遵守领域特定的业务规则，这些规则约束了何时允许执行操作以及哪些数据或资源可能受到影响。违反此类规则可能导致业务逻辑缺陷，即使任务表面上看起来已成功完成。检测这类缺陷非常困难，因为这些规则很少以明确、可测试的规范形式存在：它们一部分分散在系统提示词和工具定义中，另一部分则隐含在领域知识中。现有的智能体测试方法通常只评估任务完成情况、预定义策略或已知攻击场景，这限制了它们系统性发现先前未被明确规定的业务规则违规行为的能力。我们提出了AgenTest，它从系统提示词、工具定义和领域知识中挖掘业务规则（原摘要在此处截断）。
tldr: AgenTest通过从系统提示词、工具定义和领域知识中自动挖掘业务规则，系统性地测试LLM智能体，从而发现现有测试方法难以检测的业务逻辑缺陷。
en_tdlr: AgenTest mines business rules from system prompts, tool definitions, and domain knowledge to systematically test LLM agents and uncover business logic bugs that existing testing approaches often miss.
